report:
# Paired candidate review

Only R01 and R02 were assessed for inclusion. Both are judged **normal_or_benign** and excluded. There are zero segmented tumor instances in either examination; `events.json` consequently has no groups. This does not assert lesion disappearance or absence of tumor elsewhere.

## Method and judgments

Reviewed native axial CT images with a soft-tissue display window of −150 to 250 intensity units, successive slices above and below each center, and sagittal/coronal reformats adjusted for voxel spacing. Compared local relationships to the thyroid, clavicle, adjacent vessels and lower-neck musculature. The candidate centers were used for localization only.

| Candidate | Input | Native voxel center (i, j, k) | Judgment | Status and uncertainty |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R01 | `/app/data/baseline.nii.gz` | (304, 263, 213) | normal_or_benign | Excluded. Smooth elongated/triangular soft tissue at the left thoracic inlet, lateral to the thyroid, with tapering continuity on adjacent slices and reformats. Normal scalene-region soft tissue is favored over a discrete tumor. Moderate uncertainty in exact tissue attribution in this crowded musculovascular region. |
| R02 | `/app/data/followup.nii.gz` | (302, 221, 216) | normal_or_benign | Excluded. Similar smooth configuration and continuity at the corresponding left thoracic inlet; no separable expansile tumor identified. Normal scalene-region soft tissue is favored, with the same moderate tissue-attribution uncertainty. |

Exclusion rests on the appearance being more likely normal/benign, not on uncertainty alone. Similarity between examinations is supportive but does not by itself establish benignity. The nearby thyroid was used as an anatomical landmark, not treated as the candidate or separately segmented.

## Representative image evidence

All indices below are **zero-based native voxel indices**, not RAS world millimeters. Red ticks mark the supplied in-plane center; on neighboring slices they remain at the same in-plane coordinates.

- Baseline input `/app/data/baseline.nii.gz`: axial **k=211, 212, 213, 214** in [baseline_center.jpg](../work/baseline_center.jpg) show the smooth candidate contour and its relationship to adjacent vessels and thyroid. Serial axial **k=198–232, step 2** in [baseline_trace.jpg](../work/baseline_trace.jpg) show the changing/tapering shape through the thoracic inlet. [baseline_anatomy.jpg](../work/baseline_anatomy.jpg) supplies broader anatomical context at **k=213, 216, 219, 222, 225, 228, 231, 234**.
- Follow-up input `/app/data/followup.nii.gz`: axial **k=214, 215, 216, 217** in [followup_center.jpg](../work/followup_center.jpg) show the corresponding structure. Serial axial **k=207–229, step 2** in [followup_detail.jpg](../work/followup_detail.jpg) support continuity and the absence of a distinct nodular component.
- Orthogonal evidence: [baseline_mpr.jpg](../work/baseline_mpr.jpg) contains sagittal native **i=299, 304, 309** and coronal **j=258, 263, 268**, spanning **k=195–237**. [followup_mpr.jpg](../work/followup_mpr.jpg) contains sagittal **i=297, 302, 307** and coronal **j=216, 221, 226**, spanning **k=198–240**. These support an elongated anatomical structure rather than a discrete rounded mass. The 3-mm native slice thickness limits fine tissue separation on reformats.

## Outputs and reproducibility

Both masks are all-background, 3D uint16 NIfTI volumes. Reloaded masks were checked against their respective input for identical shape and exact affine: baseline 512×512×261; follow-up 512×512×274. Original qform/sform and voxel spacing were retained. There are no positive IDs, so the empty event list accounts for all instances.

Rendering and output scripts are preserved in `/app/work/views.py`, `/app/work/multiplanar.py`, and `/app/work/write_outputs.py`; rendered views and cached image arrays are also retained under `/app/work/`. No external images, annotations, models or network resources were used.
